newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Asian telephone operators told to be flexible.
newsitem.headline: Asian telephone operators told to be flexible.

text.p: The managing director of Siemens in Indonesia told Asian telecommunications operators on Monday to be flexible in catering to the rising demand for telephone services in the region.
Werner Schachermeir said they should be looking at technologies other than traditional copper cables in connecting people to their networks.

"The tremendous demand for telecommunications needs a fast and flexible solution for networks which can solve all conventional problems, such as geographical problems, and at the same time provide future-proof and competitive telecommunications networks," he said.

Siemens, a subsidiary of German communications firm Siemens AG, sponsored the Operator Conference on Access Network attended by 15 operators from Asian countries, including Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia, Vietnam and the Philippines.

Lothar Schmid, Siemens AG Public Communications Network general-manager, said Asia urgently needed an advanced, flexible and swift solution that provided not only a normal analog and integrated system data network, but also provided for advanced future-oriented data services.
Schmid told Reuters outside the meeting that a variety of technologies such as local wireless loop, optic fibre, copper cable and radio could all be used to access telephone networks.

"In a highly populated city like Jakarta, which has a strong demand for high- speed data transmission and multi-media services, what we offer is optical fibre cable which has a very large capacity," Schmid said.
"In other areas, maybe the most suitable one is using the wireless local loop. It really depends on the operator's needs," he said.
Schmid said the world-wide turnover of Siemens Access Network was currently around $600 million, of which roughly one-third came from Asia.
He declined to give Siemens' target for the Indonesian market.

Dadad Kustiwa, chief operations officer of Indonesian state telecommunications firm PT Telkom Indonesia, told the meeting that Access Network provided a solution for improving Telkom's current network.
"By deploying Access Network, Telkom will be able to provide sufficient technology for high-speed data transmission and multi-media services," he said.
Kustiwa said Telkom was replacing most of its copper cable network in the Jakarta business district with optical fibre cable to increase capacity and improve quality.
